description: Read the authentication headers a receiver added to one message. Headers are unfolded first, because a field continues on any line beginning with whitespace. Reports two From headers, where what is displayed and what is evaluated can differ, which is the shape of a spoof rather than a mistake; a lower Authentication-Results, which can have been written before the message arrived; a result from an untrusted server; and a DKIM or SPF domain that does not align with the From domain. Pay 200000 atomic USDC on Base via exact x402. MCP does not pay; it provides a challenge handoff.

expected_from_domain.description: The domain the From header should carry. A trailing dot is ignored, so it does not create a second name.

headers.description: The message headers as text, folded or unfolded. Nothing resolves DNS: the records are supplied, which keeps the egress surface at zero and means an arbitrary domain can be audited without this service holding an allowlist for it.
headers.example:
Received: from relay.vendor.test (relay.vendor.test [198.51.100.7])
	by mx.receiver.test with ESMTPS id abc123
	for <ada@receiver.test>; Thu, 2 Oct 2026 12:00:00 +0000
Authentication-Results: relay.vendor.test;
	spf=softfail smtp.mailfrom=bounces.vendor.test;
	dkim=pass header.d=vendor.test;
	dmarc=fail
Authentication-Results: mx.receiver.test; spf=pass smtp.mailfrom=example.test; dkim=pass header.d=example.test
From: Billing <billing@example.test>
From: Billing <billing@example-test.test>
Subject: Your invoice

trusted_authserv_ids.description: Only a result from one of these means anything, because any server upstream can write that header. Omitting it is reported as not having assessed trust.

items.description: A server whose result may be relied on. A trailing dot is ignored, so it does not create a second name.

name: email_header_authentication_audit

authenticated.description: True only when every recorded method passed, every domain aligned, and the result came from a server the caller named as trusted.

complete.description: Whether everything supplied was examined. False means part of it was not, which is a different problem from something that is wrong.

finding_count.description: The true total, even when the listing is bounded.

methods.description: Per method, the results the topmost header recorded.

passed.description: The same verdict under the name shared across the caller-supplied families.

request_id.description: Delivery request identifier; also returned in x-foundry-request-id.

title: Email Header Authentication Audit
